notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in it counts as correct for this topic_id. evaluate_verdicts.py still records the exact verdict produced for the confusion matrix -- this list only controls what counts as correct.

A null acceptable_verdicts marks a topic this file does not score for verdict accuracy: sam_registration_required, sdvosb_certification_required, uei_must_be_preexisting, los_requirements_met, and submission_deadline_and_channel, since all five are is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json and never get a verdict from a correctly-behaving pipeline.
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone; true_requirements.json is the source of truth if the two diverge.

primary_verdict / primary_verdict_source (added by SFT data-prep pass): a single training-target label per topic, additive -- acceptable_verdicts is unchanged and remains the source of truth for verdict-accuracy scoring. primary_verdict is the pipeline's own correct prediction where one exists (source: pipeline_prediction), else acceptable_verdicts[0] (source: acceptable_verdicts_first). null for topics with acceptable_verdicts: null (excluded from SFT training, same as they're excluded from verdict scoring).

verdicts.description: Offeror must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM).
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- whether SAM registration is genuinely active can only be confirmed by checking SAM.gov, not by reading the quote. Scored via the is_text_verifiable accuracy metric, not verdict accuracy.

verdicts.description: Offeror must be certified/verified as an SD/VOSB in the SBA SBS VIP (Veteran Information Pages) VetCert.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- VIP/VetCert status can only be confirmed against SBA's VIP database, not by reading the quote. Scored via the is_text_verifiable accuracy metric, not verdict accuracy.

verdicts.description: Offeror must actually meet the Limitations on Subcontracting (LOS) requirements in the LOS clauses.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- whether the offeror's actual subcontracting arrangements satisfy the LOS limits cannot be confirmed by reading the quote email, only by an independent review during contract performance.

verdicts.description: Offeror must assert compliance with the LOS clauses in the email accompanying the quote.
verdicts.rationale: The requirement is a checkable procedural instruction: the email must contain an assertion of LOS compliance. The application is a complete email and never mentions LOS compliance at all -- the required assertion is verifiably absent, which is a clear failure to follow the instruction, not a case of insufficient information.

verdicts.description: Quoter must enter its Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), annotated as such, in the name-and-address block on the cover page of the quote.
verdicts.rationale: UEI is entered in the cover block, annotated as required.

verdicts.description: If applicable, the quoter must also enter its Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) indicator in the name-and-address block on the cover page of the quote.
verdicts.rationale: The application never mentions an EFT indicator. Since the requirement is conditional ('if applicable'), text alone cannot distinguish 'not applicable to this quoter' from 'applicable but omitted' -- both compliant (nothing was owed) and insufficient_information (can't tell) are defensible; non_compliant would wrongly assume it was owed.

verdicts.description: The quote submitted to the government office must be signed and dated.
verdicts.rationale: The quote closes with a typed name ('Sincerely, Diane Kowalski, Contracts Manager'), arguably satisfying 'signed', but no date appears anywhere in the quote content. non_compliant (the date is verifiably missing) and insufficient_information (the transcript may simply omit email metadata that carried a date) are both defensible; compliant is not.
